statements.text: In terms of regulating AI, if we really wanted to take a constructive step, we would pass a federal data privacy bill. If we can’t determine who owns what data under what circumstances, then how do you regulate a technology that is fundamentally developed and driven by data? If we have to put something at the top of the list, let’s start there.
statements.venue: Americans for Responsible Innovation forum on Capitol Hill

statements.text: Deepfakes have the potential to greatly impact our ability to trust information in our daily lives. Many Americans now get much of their news from social media sites, where deepfakes and altered content can quickly proliferate, spreading misinformation and lies. It’s essential that the government consider how to best respond to misleading or malicious content created by artificial intelligence, while ensuring we do not infringe on individual freedom of speech or expression.
statements.venue: Press release on House Intelligence Committee deepfakes hearing

statements.text: The US Government is often slow off the mark in technological development, but with the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence it’s more important than ever that we keep pace with our adversaries. The AI PLAN Act is an important step towards ensuring that our Administration is equipped to counter threats to our markets and protect Americans from financial crimes.
statements.venue: Press release on AI PLAN Act introduction (Nunn/Himes)

statements.text: Meanwhile, the AI companies may not be in total agreement, but they are begging the government to step in and lead. They see real danger ahead. Three Thoughts: 3/7

The Speaker gave the game away: Congressional Republicans cannot IMAGINE leading on any regulation. And Trump, who probably doesn’t know what AI stands for, is beholden to whatever billionaire techdroid last  stood behind the Resolute. 2/7

I watched Speaker Johnson on the Sunday shows this morning  make yet another set of excuses for Congressional inaction on AI. The doozy was this: the AI companies don’t agree on the regulation they want. What the hell? 1/7 🧵

Scammers have always been a contemptible part of our financial reality, but AI-powered voice cloning and deepfakes have turbo-charged the tools they have at their disposal to swindle Americans – especially seniors – out of their hard-earned money,

statements.text: I don’t know if this reporting is accurate but I intend to find out. I do know that AI is tremendously powerful but it can also be tremendously dangerous. Making sure we employ these tools in a smart way that keeps a human in the loop is a day one priority for House Democrats.
